# `set_camera_16bit`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Select the camera pixel format via a boolean (behaviour on the audited backend is unusual).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xcefe0, SetBytesPerPix @0x11e850 (64-bit build); SDK image-type enum, gained 8-bit conversion helpers and cropped-capture type check from the camera library debug information; 32-bit build set_camera_16bit JSON boolean type check and bytes-per-pixel set/get switches in the camera class; 32-bit statically linked backend image fetch dispatches to the same helper family |

Required boolean. The handler passes 0 (false) or 1 (true) to the backend, which accepts only 1 or 2; it maps 1 to format enum 3 and 2 to format enum 2. Consequently on the audited 64-bit camera backend false is rejected with 210 and true selects format enum 3 (get_camera_16bit then reports false, because it tests for enum 2). The 32-bit build behaves the same way end to end (READ, 32-bit build); it also requires a JSON boolean (106 otherwise), maps true to format 3, refuses false with 210 and gives 318 with no camera. The image types are 1 (8-bit raw), 2 (16-bit raw; 10- or 12-bit samples widened, with hot-pixel correction) and 3 (8-bit Bayer mosaic; black level subtracted, red/blue white-balance gains applied, scaled to 8 bits and clipped at 255; not debayered, one byte per pixel). Cropped capture supports only format 3. So true selects 8-bit capture, not 16-bit (READ, 64-bit camera library; INFERRED for the 32-bit camera backend); a client MUST NOT infer bit depth from this flag.

Side effects: Stores the camera pixel-format selection in the camera object.

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 106 | Params missing, empty array, null or not a boolean (integers rejected) | `expected bool param` |
| 318 | Camera is closed | `device not connected` |
| 210 | Backend rejects the value (false, on both builds) | `not supported` |
| 207 | Operation failure whose thread-local error code is zero (the default substituted when the callee set none); other callee-set codes are forwarded unchanged | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

The accepted value selects pixel format 3 (gained 8-bit Bayer) on both builds; false gives 210 on both.

## Example

Request, false - Rejected on the audited backend (shape INFERRED):

```json
{"id":51,"method":"set_camera_16bit","params":false}
```

Request, true:

```json
{"id":52,"method":"set_camera_16bit","params":true}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_camera_16bit","error":"not supported","code":210,"id":51}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_camera_16bit","result":0,"code":0,"id":52}
```
